text:
**Short answer: for most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station uses it, and the sources agree on why.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated 3,000 to 6,000 cycles; NMC models are rated roughly 500 to 800 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). At one full cycle a day, that's about 1.4 years for a 500-cycle NMC unit versus about 8 years for a 3,000-cycle LFP unit. Check the rating's end point (80% vs 70%) and the test conditions, since brands don't all measure it the same way.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab studies, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently than NMC cells. But it's not fireproof, and one study found LFP reached runaway sooner in overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Use approved chargers and follow the manual either way.
- **Cost:** One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC, and per rated cycle LFP is far cheaper ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells store more energy per pound, but the gap mostly shrinks in finished stations because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% difference in median Wh per lb, and the Anker SOLIX C1000 (LFP) is lighter per Wh than the Goal Zero Yeti 1000 Lithium (NMC) ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare actual model specs.

**Cold weather:** This is less clear-cut than some sites claim. Manuals for both chemistries generally say don't charge below 32°F, and limits depend more on the maker than the chemistry ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check your model's manual.

**When NMC is fine:** a rarely used unit (a few outages or weekends a year), a weight-sensitive carry, or a working NMC unit you already own. For occasional use, calendar aging matters more than cycle count.

**A buying example (LFP):** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating, a 5-year warranty, and ≤15 ms UPS switchover. It's listed at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF per the listing (tested 2026-10-24, so confirm at checkout). It isn't expandable, and the link is an affiliate link. It's one example, not a recommendation for your needs. Size the station to what you need to run (watts and watt-hours) first, and chemistry second.
